elements.quote: Overall, in 79 studies in a range of different settings, 20% (95% confidence interval [CI] 17%-25%, prediction interval 3%-67%) of people with SARS-CoV-2 infection remained asymptomatic during follow-up, but biases in study designs limit the certainty of this estimate. In seven studies of defined populations screened for SARS-CoV-2 and then followed, 31% (95% CI 26%-37%, prediction interval 24%-38%) remained asymptomatic.
elements.reason: It reports the total number of included studies (79) and provides summary information for relevant study characteristics/settings (range of settings; seven defined populations).

elements.quote: Overall, in 79 studies in a range of different settings, 20% (95% confidence interval [CI] 17%-25%, prediction interval 3%-67%) of people with SARS-CoV-2 infection remained asymptomatic during follow-up ... In seven studies of defined populations screened for SARS-CoV-2 and then followed, 31% (95% CI 26%-37%, prediction interval 24%-38%) remained asymptomatic. Wefound some evidence that SARS-CoV-2 infection in contacts of people with asymptomatic infection is less likely than in contacts of people with symptomatic infection (relative risk 0.35, 95% CI 0.10-1.27).
elements.reason: It presents results for main outcomes, including key summary estimates with CIs for asymptomatic infection and a comparative effect (relative risk) for contacts.

elements.quote: There is disagreement about the level of asymptomatic severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection.
elements.reason: The review describes the current state of knowledge by stating there is disagreement about the level of asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection.

elements.quote: The proportion of people who will remain asymptomatic throughout the course of infection with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), the cause of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), is not known.
elements.reason: The importance/need is explained by identifying that the proportion remaining asymptomatic is not known.

elements.quote: We found three systematic reviews, which reported similar summary estimates from meta-analysis of studies published up to May [119-121]. In two reviews, authors applied inclusion criteria to reduce the risks of selection bias, with summary estimates of 11% (95% CI 4%-18%, 6 studies) [120] and 15% (95% CI 12%-18%, 9 studies) [121]. Our review includes all these studies, mostly in the categories of aggregated contact or outbreak investigations, with compatible summary estimates (Fig 1).
elements.reason: When similar systematic reviews exist, the need for the current review is explained by comparing with prior systematic reviews and stating how the current review relates/includes those studies.

No proposed mechanism of action is described because the review is not presented as an intervention-effects review; the retrieved evidence focuses on estimating proportions and transmission related to asymptomatic/presymptomatic infection.

A logic model for hypothesised relationships between intervention components and outcomes is not considered applicable because the retrieved evidence does not describe a complex intervention or delivery context requiring a logic model.

elements.quote: The objectives of this study were to address three questions: (1) Amongst people who become infected with SARS-CoV-2, what proportion do not experience symptoms at all during their infection? (2) Amongst people with SARS-CoV-2 infection who are asymptomatic when diagnosed, what proportion will develop symptoms later? (3) What proportion of SARS-CoV-2 transmission is accounted for by people who are either asymptomatic throughout infection or presymptomatic?
elements.reason: The review objectives/questions are explicitly stated as three clear questions.

elements.quote: We conducted a living systematic review and metaanalysis to address three questions: (1) Amongst people who become infected with SARSCoV-2, what proportion does not experience symptoms at all during their infection? (2) Amongst people with SARS-CoV-2 infection who are asymptomatic when diagnosed, what proportion will develop symptoms later? (3) What proportion of SARS-CoV-2 transmission is accounted for by people who are either asymptomatic throughout infection or presymptomatic?
elements.reason: The stated objectives are proportion/transmission questions rather than planned intervention comparisons, so PICO (or an appropriate variant for intervention effects) is not applicable.

elements.quote: Weincluded studies in any language of people with SARS-CoV-2 diagnosed by RT-PCR that documented follow-up and symptom status at the beginning and end of follow-up or investigated the contribution to SARS-CoV-2 transmission of asymptomatic or presymptomatic infection. We included contact-tracing investigations, case series, cohort studies, case-control studies, and statistical and mathematical modelling studies.
elements.reason: Eligibility characteristics are described for population (RT-PCR diagnosed SARS-CoV-2), follow-up and symptom-status timing (beginning and end of follow-up), and study designs. However, the evidence does not clearly specify other requested components such as eligible settings and follow-up requirements beyond documenting symptom status at beginning/end.

No explicit eligibility criteria are provided for report characteristics such as dissemination year, language requirements (beyond a statement 'any language' which is part of this criterion but lacks year and publication/report status), or publication vs report status. Therefore, required report-characteristic eligibility criteria are not fully specified.
The conditional distinction between excluding because outcomes were not measured versus excluding because outcome results were not reported is not described in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The reviewers determined which of the three review questions each study addressed, using the definitions in Box 1.
elements.reason: The review describes grouping by assigning each study to one of three review questions. However, it does not explicitly state how these groups are linked to specific comparisons defined in the review objectives (the retrieved evidence does not include the objective-comparison structure).
Rationales for notable restrictions (e.g., the specific study-type exclusions) are not provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The review first search on 25 March 2020 and updated it on 20 April and 10 June 2020.
elements.reason: The dates when the information sources were last searched/updated are reported (25 March 2020; updated 20 April and 10 June 2020).

elements.quote: Wesearched the COVID-19 living evidence database [10], which is generated using automated workflow processes [5] to (1) provide daily updates of searches of four electronic databases (Medline PubMed, Ovid Embase, bioRxiv, and medRxiv), using medical subject headings and free-text keywords for SARS-CoV-2 infection and COVID-19; (2) de-duplicate the records; (3) tag records that are preprints; and (4) allow searches of titles and abstracts using Boolean operators. We used the search function to identify studies of asymptomatic or presymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection using a search string of medical subject headings and free-text keywords (S1 Text).
elements.reason: The evidence explains that searches use MeSH/free-text and Boolean operators and that a specific search string is in S1 Text, but it does not cite published search approaches/filters with described adaptations.

elements.quote: The primary outcomes for each review question were (1) proportion with asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection who did not experience symptoms at all during follow-up; (2) proportion with SARS-CoV-2 infections who did not have symptoms at the time of testing but developed symptoms during follow-up; (3) estimated proportion (with uncertainty interval) of SARS-CoV-2 transmission accounted for by people who are asymptomatic or presymptomatic. A secondary outcome for review question 3 was the secondary attack rate from asymptomatic or presymptomatic index cases.
elements.reason: All outcome domains for which data were sought are enumerated (asymptomatic, presymptomatic, transmission proportion, and secondary attack rate) and described as primary/secondary outcomes.

elements.quote: The end of follow-up was defined as any of the following: virological cure, with one or more negative reverse transcriptase PCR (RT-PCR) test results; follow-up for 14 days or more after the last possible exposure to an index case; follow-up for 7 days or more after the first RT-PCR positive result.
elements.reason: A specific time frame for symptom status/outcome measurement is defined via the paper’s definition of “end of follow-up”.

elements.quote: The extracted variables included, but were not limited to, study design, country and/or region, study setting, population, age, primary outcomes, and length of follow-up.

elements.quote: If there were no events in a group, we added 0.5 to each cell in the 2 × 2 table. We used random-effects meta-analysis with the Mantel-Haenszel method to estimate a summary risk ratio (with 95% CI).
elements.reason: The review describes specific methods for preparing/synthesizing data for presentation, including handling zero-event cells by applying a continuity correction prior to meta-analysis.

elements.quote: We examined heterogeneity visually in forest plots. To synthesise proportions from comparable studies, in terms of design and population, we used stratified random-effects meta-analysis. For the stratified and overall summary estimates, we calculated prediction intervals...
elements.reason: The review describes synthesis-preparation steps for calculating summary estimates (stratified random-effects meta-analysis and prediction intervals), specifying how study results were prepared for pooled presentation.

elements.quote:
Social distancing measures will need to be sustained at some level because droplet transmission from close contact with people with asymptomatic and presymptomatic infection occurs.
Easing of restrictions will, however, only be possible with wide access to testing, contact tracing, and rapid isolation of infected individuals.
Quarantine of close contacts is also essential to prevent onward transmission during asymptomatic or presymptomatic periods of those that have become infected.
Digital, proximity tracing could supplement classical contact tracing to speed up detection of contacts to interrupt transmission during the presymptomatic phase if shown to be effective [19,127].
The findings of this systematic review of publications early in the pandemic suggests that most SARS-CoV-2 infections are not asymptomatic throughout the course of infection. The contribution of presymptomatic and asymptomatic infections to overall SARS-CoV-2 transmission means that combination prevention measures, with enhanced hand and respiratory hygiene, testing tracing, and isolation strategies and social distancing, will continue to be needed.
elements.reason: The discussion provides practical/operational implications, specifying prevention measures (hygiene, masks/social distancing implied, testing, contact tracing, isolation, quarantine) that should continue to be used.
